title: This Bird Flew 8,400 Miles Without Landing. Eleven Days Straight

scenes.text: This bird flew 8,400 miles without landing. Eleven days.
A bar-tailed godwit, five months old. Alaska to Tasmania, October 2022. Tracked by satellite.
No food, no water, no landing. It flapped the whole way; godwits don't glide.
It crossed the entire Pacific, over islands it could have stopped on. It didn't.
For fuel, it digests a quarter of its own gut, liver and kidneys, and grows a bigger heart mid flight.
It lands having lost maybe half its body weight. Eleven days. 8,400 miles.

description:
In October 2022, a five-month-old bar-tailed godwit flew 13,560 kilometres, about 8,400 miles, nonstop from Alaska to Tasmania in 11 days and 1 hour, the longest nonstop bird flight ever tracked.
Godwits flap the whole way rather than glide, don't stop to eat or drink, and fuel the trip by breaking down about a quarter of their own digestive tract, liver and kidneys while enlarging their heart and chest muscles. The bird probably lost half or more of its body weight.
What's the longest you've ever travelled without stopping? Comment below.
first_comment: The previous record, 13,050 km, was set by an adult godwit in 2021; this one beat it as a five-month-old on its first ever migration. Would you rather be able to fly for 11 days or hold your breath for 3 hours like a whale?
